steps.name: Agent A
steps.text: No sudden moves.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: You know, I'm sure we can talk about this like reasonable people—

steps.name: Agent A
steps.text: All the rioters are here.

steps.name: Agent B
steps.text: Shut them in the lower level jail. We'll hand them to the courts when we arrive in D.C.

steps.name: Agent B
steps.text: It's almost time. Double-check your parachutes unless you want to end up in a puddle.

steps.name: Agent B
steps.text: What? Did someone press the detonate button early?

steps.name: Agent A
steps.text: Impossible! We're less than a kilometer from the District... Wait, the government buildings are getting smaller... we're moving away from the capital?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Looks like events are moving faster than your plans can catch up, aren't they?

steps.name: Agent B
steps.text: You never intended to stop the explosion... you were just stalling for time for the plate to turn?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Did you think we had the means to go toe-to-toe with well-trained units?

steps.name: Agent B
steps.text: Events moving faster than the plans can catch up...

steps.name: Agent B
steps.text: Change of plans.

steps.name: Agent B
steps.text: Lower level, evacuate by the planned routes. Upper level, protect the civilians around you and prepare to parachute.

steps.name: Agent B
steps.text: Point Zero, detonate.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: What's going on? The broadcast has gone dark... are the screens outside getting a signal?

steps.name: Tester
steps.text: You're still thinking about the broadcast?! Didn't you hear the Emergency Management Council's evacuation warning?

steps.name: Tester
steps.text: A serious accident has occurred in the levitation layer. All floating facilities will fall from the sky in less than ten minutes! Hurry up and get yourself to the emergency shelters!

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: Fall from the sky...?
Oakley looks up to see hundreds of floating pods turn into fireballs in the sky, marring the clear skies with smoke and ash.
Without the gentle touch of sunlight, the cloud-like pods turn back into chunks of metal, crashing down on the lower level.
Look out.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: *cough*... that was a close call. Thanks.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: You're a tester? Which company? I don't remember you...

steps.name: Tester?
steps.text: Now is not the time for introductions, Oakley.

steps.name: Tester?
steps.text: The streets are exposed. You risk getting hit by falling debris. You should go into an emergency shelter quickly.

steps.name: Oakley
steps.text: A-Alright...
Falling.
Tumbling down.
Ferne's heart is beating so hard, she feels like it might escape her ribcage at any moment.
She tries her best to control her breathing. The straps on the sides of the helmet slap her face, inflicting just enough pain to fend off the fear of falling.
In an instant, the signal from the detonator travels through the connected conduits, igniting all the floating facilities at the same time. Ferne leaps from Platform 7 before it loses all power.
The falling pod streaks past Ferne like a black meteor.
The bright-colored paint is burned off the advertisements, and melted cables flail in the air, giving off a bitter smell of tar.
The whole levitation layer sways meekly in the air like a deflated balloon.
'Lucky Cystybeast', 'One-Boot', 'Beachbrella'...
Ferne watches these company logos fall together with her. Now that is a scene that rivals sunset in the Bleached Wasteland, she thinks.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Pull the parachute, Ferne!

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Oops, almost forgot.
The updraft lifts the Feline's slender frame. The parachutes come together to form a massive cloud.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Did we do it?

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: The people on the ground don't know what's happening. It must be a shock for them to see their investments and products turn to ash...

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: They're safe, at least. The pieces of the levitation layer would have fallen on top of their heads if the plate didn't turn around.

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Besides, they'll never find out that there were scheming and plotting to stop them from dreaming.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Where do we go next?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: You could certainly go back to Northville to see your wife.

steps.name: Aspen
steps.text: Sure. What about after that?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: After that?

steps.name: Ferne
steps.text: Let's talk about that when we get back to standing on Terra Firma and looking up at the sky.
The light of burning fire illuminates the people's faces, but there is little regret in their hearts as they gaze upon Propeller Paradise, now beyond recognition.
The remains of Propeller Paradise are scattered across the barrenlands between the District and the plate, like gifts that have been returned.
Ferne closes her eyes in relaxation, as she comes back down to earth with paradise.
The elderly Banshee said her kin were like broken kites as they fell burning from the sky in that war from two hundred years ago.
Now, though, she is like a kite that has too many strings attached, the branches and roots tugging at her as she floats in mid-air.
A kite nothing could ever ruin, as she had wished.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: The Roosting Tree... that was the name I gave it. I built huts beneath it, and made it the abode of every Banshee.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: But all I felt was fear when Laqeramaline brought me to its roots.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: It was like a great void that could not be illuminated by the moons, by candles, or by fireflies. It was still and silent, sucking away my memory a little bit at a time...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I could smell decay in the darkness. A decay that we could not reverse. Not even the Children of Soil and Stone could.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: It was a constant reminder of how pathetic the Convallis was.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: At the end, Lady Theresa and Lord Theresis found a future for the Sarkaz through war and death. Meanwhile, Aefanyl continues to seek a new future for the Banshees.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: But me and my valley... it is nothing more than a failed sanctuary that quietly awaits death.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: And there's nothing more I can do for it.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: So you ran away from the Roosting Tree, ran away from death.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Why here, though?

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Everywhere outside the Convallis was the same. Grey and chaotic, impossible to navigate.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: There was only one path that I remembered. Those unfamiliar names that you said... Leithanien, Laterano, Columbia...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I followed the names, followed your scent, not knowing to what end the path lead, and what I would do there... I just didn't want the tree to turn me into an empty husk.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: But you chose to go into another tree.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I was filled with sorrow when I saw that you planted another Roosting Tree here.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: When I felt the spread of decay... I thought you were going to repeat our mistakes.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Even if we couldn't save the Convallis's Roosting Tree... I wanted to do something for this one.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Even if all I could do was stay its decay and save you from sorrow for a while...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: But when I saw it with my own eyes, I realized... there was nothing I could do for it... but it could save me.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: The Roosting Tree only takes memories, but this one shares.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: It shares the story of the Convallis, and of your journey... it makes me feel that I'm alive.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I'm sorry, Nasti. I had fused with the tree before I stopped the path from collapsing. Once again... I deceived you.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: ...That's why you're so lucid.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: That's why the tree rejects my incantations. You rewrote its grammar and changed its operating logic.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It keeps you alive, and you keep it running, even though neither of you are what you used to be.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You're like a program that relies on a bug to keep running...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Bug...? Program...?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Like a withered tree that relies on a parasitic vine to remain standing.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: It's not so bad, is it?

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: If this can keep it from withering, then I've finally done something useful, for you, for the Banshees, for Sarkaz.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I can bring it back to the Convallis... bring you back.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: That would be pointless.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Why... why is the tree not responding to me?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: That means it's working.

The outer casing of the device Nasti is carrying on her belt falls away with a crack. Paper tapes pour out, laying themselves out around her as though following an invisible blueprint, forming an elaborate and organized framework.
The tapes are filled with tiny holes that represent incantations, coming together to build Nasti's unique language and safeguard her unique rules, rejecting the anarchic spread of the branches.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I said I must understand, before I can put an end to this error.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Now, I do.
Nasti raises her pen and writes down a function, an incantation.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: (Speaks in Sarkaz) Reconstruct.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: No... the memories that the tree shared with me... they're disappearing...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Nasti... Nasti! What are you doing?!

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Wiping the preloaded data in the tree. All that it shared with you was only temporary data for experimentation.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I know that you don't want to forget. But what you truly want to remember and retain are not these hotchpotch data put together for experiments.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Even if it's so...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Please, don't make the last thing I see be the sight of you destroying your life's work...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: You've walked such a long road and suffered so much for it...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: To you, the Convallis was your life's work. But I've never had one.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I have a goal. This tree is the means to it.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: My judgment of it is not based on how much I committed to it, only whether it can achieve my goal.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You hoped that fusing with it would keep it from withering. But not withering won't make it any more useful.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Just like the Roosting Tree of the Convallis.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I don't want to be cruel, but the Roosting Tree never truly consoled the dying. It is no more than a simple phoebe tree, bent under the weight of incantations.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It's native to the genus Phoebopsis in the family of Targangils-Simaroubaceae, and its wood is commonly used for buildings in southeast Terra. I had an Elf colleague verify its nature after I joined Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It became the Roosting Tree of the Convallis because you saw it as a symbol and mourned its change.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It has withered because it has reached the end of its natural lifespan.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: That is... all...?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Even the colors that run through its branches is merely the result of exposure to incantations over the years.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I don't remember how it used to look anymore...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: But... Nasti... if it's truly so...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Why does your tree look so much like the Roosting Tree?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Because it reminds me of you.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Just as you think of me.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Do you know why I planted this 'tree'?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I remember the day we parted.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You were calling to me, but I didn't turn back, because some words can no longer be said once you see the other person's face. But I couldn't help but look at your face reflected in the water—

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I wanted to remember how you looked.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: New tears flow across the lines made by old ones, as though it was a fixture on your face.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I spent more than a decade with you in the Convallis. I never saw you without tear marks on your face.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Life in the valley was good. I would have chosen the Convallis over Kazdel every time, a hundred times over. But Væla...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Was there a single moment that you weren't in pain, over the course of your two hundred years in the Convallis?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: At first, I thought I could wipe away your tears and make you smile with simple methods.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: You spent a whole day wiping my face with mistapple pulp.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It was only later that I learned why you were in pain.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The source of your pain was the decision, the lie.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The kin who suffered because they defied their nature; the kindred who could not return to the myriad souls because there was no one to deliver them. They were the source of your pain.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: To solve your problem, I must solve the problems of the Banshees, the problems of the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The answer lies outside the Convallis, outside Kazdel, in a place that I don't know.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: As I indulged in such fantasies...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I saw you and I sail in the sky.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: The reflected sky...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It was a calm, windless day, but suddenly the water rippled without warning, wiping away the eternal tear marks on your face. You almost looked like you were smiling.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: And so, I began to think about the sky whenever I thought about how to make you smile.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Perhaps...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The sky is where we can find our sanctuary, and abode for our souls.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: (Speaks in Sarkaz) The Sarkaz's promised land could also be in the sky.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: All the things you did, this tree in the sky...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: That's where it all began.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Access security camera image.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Falling... like a broken kite...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Looks like Maylander successfully carried out their plan. The entire capital will bear witness to the fall of Propeller Paradise.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: But the tremors came from the ground plate. Did Gordon...?

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Will we fall too?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Not sure. I've undone the fusion and reset the tree, restoring it to an operable state.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: But the tree itself is not yet complete.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: At least... save yourself, Nasti...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Three years ago, Aefanyl added a condition to my hypothesis when he delivered the myriad souls. Two years ago, a friend split the sky and showed me the path to the future.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: But I'm still one step away from the answer. What is to come will depend on whether we find it.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: We're in the sky, but... I don't see the answer.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Everything has fallen... they sky is empty.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Yes, the sky has always been empty.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It is we who must fill it.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: For you, Væla, I don't think the answer is in the sky.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It's in you.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I can hear the roars, the hatred, the cries that surround you.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: The kin I delivered, or failed to deliver... Vampires, Nachzehrers, Djaj... and Banshees.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I've wiped all the preloaded temporary experiment data from the tree.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: It's your own frustration, rage and sorrow that binds you now, like every Banshee that you sent away the last two hundred years, like every Sarkaz that returned to the myriad souls since the beginning of time.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: That is why our people are made empty by painful oblivion. That is why the myriad souls are always roaring, always angry, always wailing.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: But if we leave behind residues of information in death, and the myriad souls are merely the collective of such residues...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Why shouldn't it be joy and song that remains?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Does our nature prevent it?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: To process residues of information, build a server. If coverage on the ground isn't enough, raise it into the sky.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Not just a sanctuary for the living; the 'tree' will become an abode for the departed as well. This time, however, we decide what we leave behind.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Perhaps it wasn't function that the 'tree' was missing. It was a command, a decision, a sincere wish.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Tell me the answer, Væla. What is it that you truly want to leave behind?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: The tree... I will preserve that memory for you.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Oblivion will never claim what you want to leave behind.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I don't know.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You don't know...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: At first, I just wanted to save our kin from pain, from anger, from sorrow.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: But I no longer know how that can be achieved. If neither the Convallis nor the Roosting Tree could accomplish it... is there any meaning in leaving anything behind?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Væla...
Nasti wanted to do something, say something, but no sound comes out from her lips.
She is normally not one to deal with hypotheticals, but she could not help but think: If she finished the tree and took her people to the sanctuary in the sky sooner...
Would her mother have had a comforting memory to cling to?
Hundreds of pods fall burning from the sky, like black meteors, like heavy raindrops, like broken kites.
Mother and daughter gaze at each other silently, as they hoped it would make this moment an eternity.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: You were never one to stop walking, Nasti. Once you've decided on a path, you'll see it through to the end.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Don't stop now. Don't let me take away the meaning of what you've accomplished. My life may have had no meaning, but there must be some meaning to all that you've done...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: If this tree is the new abode for the souls of the Sarkaz, then let me be its first denizen.

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I gave you a home twenty years ago. Now, you've given me one.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: When the children stand around the tree to listen to its voice... I want it to be your laughter that they hear, not your weeping.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: And I want to remember your smile when I think of you...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: Nasti, my child...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I've had good memories... memories that made me smile...

steps.name: Væla
steps.text: I remember... it was...
She cannot finish the sentence.
Half a year has passed since she realized that she was beginning to forget, and fled her hut under the Roosting Tree, following Nasti's trail all the way to Columbia.
A journey far too long for a dying Banshee.
It was not the reunion that she had hoped for. But as the obsession that carried her to this point falls apart, death has finally caught up to her.
Countless scenes fade from Væla's memories, and become vivid before Nasti's eyes.

a.text: The Banshee's oar lies still in her hands.
She hears a lament. The king who painted the same dream with her has passed, in a faraway place that she cannot see.
The Banshee stands still beneath the Roosting Tree.
She spent three months witnessing her kin fall victim to oblivion and become an empty husk, the price they paid for her lies, and there was nothing she could do about it.
The Banshee kneels still on the floor of a dilapidated house.
She promised to deliver a Gargoyle who helped her in the past, but all that was left was the tip of a petrified tail.
The Banshee's sorrow and regrets are infinite, flowing past Nasti like a river without end.
After all of these memories have faded, there is one last thing that is left. One tiny, brief fragment.
The Banshee is putting a child to bed, a girl whom she brought back to the Convallis.
Her eyes are filled with fatigue as she looks at her old friend, but all she would talk about is how lovely the child is.
She used to be a child, once.
She opens her eyes and sees this land for the first time. She does not know whether it is good or bad.
But Nasti can see that she is smiling.

steps.text: Time passes through the Banshee, like the wind across the surface of Mist Lake, leaving nothing behind.
Væla fades away into the sky.
A leaf gently drifts down.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: I'll catch you, and remember you...

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Mother.
Nasti catches the leaf gently, as her mother once picked a leaf from the tree for her.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: ...One does not need a bone whistle to accompany a smile.
After a long silence, she blows a tune with the leaf.
Like threads, the notes weave the gentlest incantation that she has ever weaved.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Be at peace.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I'd like to make a bet with you, Miss Wilson.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: How many sky stocks do you think young Pavard, that honest and serious secretary of mine, will go and buy once he delivers the balloons?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Zero. The end of the line at the stock exchange was two blocks away when I came.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: The last time I saw this level of excitement in the District was when the Department of Defense decided to send troops to Bolívar. I still have one of those cactus hats in my office.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: People went into the streets wearing those hats, shouting slogans and turning the veins of the D.C. green.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I haven't seen those hats in a long time.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: No one wants their taxes turn into guns, not since Robert McKesson and his feat of 'saving Bolívar from the Bolívarians' became the butt of evening radio's jokes.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Everybody wears a propeller on their heads now.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: A blue propeller hat that spins. It's awfully noisy, to tell the truth.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I hear there's a new version that automatically plays that rock song every Columbian knows when the propeller spins.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I grew up listening to 'Terra Bless Us' and 'Cityway 66'. I once thought that the song of our time would be 'Goodnight, Arc-01.'

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Turns out it would be 'Good Night, Kristen Wright.'

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: The obsession that Columbians have with the future will never change, but the one they're following seems to have changed while we weren't looking.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Kristen never intended to become an idol.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: The Department of Defense never intended to become a joke.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: It never occurred to any of us, when we raised a glass to the failure of the DOD, that it wouldn't be just the DOD who loses credibility.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: The people listening to late-night radio over a pot of mac & cheese don't differentiate between the DOD, Congress, or the cabinet, after all.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: As you said yourself, these days, the masses seem more willing to take inspiration from a legend or miracle.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Sometimes, however, we need to turn their gazes back to the soil that nurtures miracle.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Back to Columbia.

steps.name: Tech Review Reporter
steps.text: Finally, we lay our eyes on Propeller Paradise. Not a day has passed that we don't think about it, ever since that fateful night two years ago...

steps.name: The Savior Special Guest
steps.text: The synchronized aerial turn that we just witnessed is a testament to the skill of our test pilots, even in times of peace.

steps.name: Voice of Progress Official Channel
steps.text: Now, Propeller Paradise reveals its miracles to use, this wonderful spectacle of the Columbian Dream—

steps.name: Tech Review Reporter
steps.text: Demonstrating that—

steps.name: The Savior Special Guest
steps.text: Declaring that—
Silence.
Every media outlet, every channel, voices rich or coarse or sharp or warm, all fall silent at the same time.
The entrepreneurs and investors on the streets, along with thousands upon thousands of ordinary people, fall silent too.
For a few minutes, the only sound in Max, D.C. is the sound of their propeller hats.
The rustling sound they make, like falling leaves, is the only accompaniment to this spectacular disaster, witnessed by millions in the capital.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: ...'turn their gazes back to the soil that nurtures miracle.'

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Back to Columbia.

steps.name: Voice of Progress Official Channel
steps.text: A terrorist attack?

steps.name: Tech Review Reporter
steps.text: ...A premeditated act of terror.

steps.name: The Savior Special Guest
steps.text: Investigators confirm that the explosion was caused by a batch of Arts weapons smuggled in disguised as general parts.

steps.name: The Savior Special Guest
steps.text: The weapons can be traced to numerous centrum nations, including...

steps.name: Tech Review Reporter
steps.text: Kazimierz, which has long since abandoned the ways of chivalry, and Leithanien, the ancient nation of casters, have used their despicable tricks against us.

steps.name: Voice of Progress Official Channel
steps.text: The voice of progress falls silent today. It is the darkest day in Columbia's eighty years of history...

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: The nation is waiting for me to speak.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I should tell them: 'They have destroyed more than just an exhibition; they have destroyed the hopes and dreams that every Columbian entrusted to it.'

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I should tell them: 'This shameless, heinous act was committed by those who envy our splendor, trying to make our people timid and afraid.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I should tell them: 'But they're doomed to fail. Columbia will never be defeated. No conspiracy can stop the Lamp and Star from shining bright in the west.'

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: And then, Columbians will eagerly turn their taxes into guns again?

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Everything that they fervently devoted to Propeller Paradise, all those sky stocks, and the spinning propeller hats, will turn into shields and swords.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: When the smoke clears, the empty sky will be more inflammatory than any speech.
The winds on the wilderness of Columbia have never stopped, mercilessly blowing away the smoke and cloud that surrounded Propeller Paradise.
The sky feels even emptier than before, after all things bright and beautiful have fallen.
But it's not entirely empty.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Is the soot playing tricks on my eyes?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I see it as well as you do, Mr. Vice President.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: As do millions of people here in D.C.
Floating platforms supported by a complicated system of massive hot-air balloons and propellers have fallen. Floating labs of many shapes and sizes have fallen.

The ropeway system that connected the levitation layer has fallen, along with hundreds of pods. The saucer-shaped tower that linked the ground and the sky has fallen, along with the elevator that it supports.
Only one thing rises through the clouds, into the bright skies of Columbia.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: Message from Maylander, sir.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: Propeller Paradise has stopped moving toward the capital. It is now headed for the southeastern border, accelerating.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: Maylander believes they are trying to escape Columbia, which would be an act of treason.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: Mechanized units on the border are moving to cut off Propeller Paradise's potential routes.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: More importantly, the unknown object in the sky has already been locked on by our defensive artillery deployed along the District's route.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: With your speech about to begin, they want to hear how you define it.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: The Department of Defense recommends opening fire immediately, and sticking with the current narrative. Maylander has raised the possibility of conveying a different message through the survival of this facility.

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: But they have also noted the risks of doing so. The facility was created by Rhine Lab, after all.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Before they do anything, I would like to get a good look at this thing myself.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: A tree?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: A tree.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Rhine certainly has style, doesn't it? A tree-shaped facility. Do you know what it is?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I have no idea. I suppose I'm just here to lighten the mood while you vent about Rhine.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Heh. Well, it doesn't matter.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: What it is will soon stop mattering to the people, just like that balloon that couldn't fly.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: In the DOD's game, it will become an infant slaughtered by knights, an envoy killed by the Witch King. Its fall will drive the rise of the people's wrath.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: In Maylander's proposal, it will become the next symbol of the Columbian spirit, its silhouette printed on every hat that leaves the factories for the next decade.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Is that so? All I see is a tree.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: You see those fowlbeasts, brushing their feathers and honing their beaks?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: They've accepted that it's a tree. A tree that they can roost on.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: A tree rising from the wounds of Columbia? How should people understand it?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: They don't have to.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Just as you didn't need to understand the mobile mining platform on the wilderness that you skipped classes to watch when you were young.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Did you know if it was carrying a group of ambitious pioneers, or desperate debtors? Did it return with a full load of riches, or was it simply drifting aimlessly?

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: All I know is that I really didn't want to take a test that day, and the mining platform happened to be chasing the setting sun.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: A mining platform chasing the setting sun, and a flying tree.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: They're not so different, are they?

steps.name: Vice President's Secretary
steps.text: What is your position, Mr. Vice President?

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I'm the vice president of the Columbian Union. With this position, comes responsibility.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I can't skip classes to watch a mining platform chase the setting sun, like I used to.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: Still...

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: That was, indeed, what made me feel something about the soil of Columbia for the first time.

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: If the sky is the soil that nurtures the future of Columbia...

steps.name: Jackson
steps.text: I'm sure there's enough room in it for a flying tree.
